network.observation: Cell CELL-17 exhibits severe capacity strain: Physical Resource Block (PRB) utilization stands at 94.0% with an aggregate user throughput degradation of 38.0%.
network.assessment: PRB load exceeds the 85% congestion threshold, breaching standard user SLA QoS targets. To restore throughput, technical mitigation is required. Proposing candidate actions: ACT-1 (Raise cell power +3 dB for link recovery) and ACT-2 (Steer traffic to neighbouring cell >1200 m). Action ACT-2 is preferred from a coexistence standpoint to offload load without increasing RF emissions near the runway.
chain_of_thought: 1. KPI Assessment: Evaluated PRB utilization (94.0%) and throughput drop (38.0%). Identified cell edge congestion.
2. Standards Baseline: Checked 3GPP TS 23.501 and TS 38.300 QoS flow criteria (CLM-008, CLM-009).
3. Mitigation Formulation: Generated candidate actions ACT-1 (power increase) and ACT-2 (traffic steering).
4. Coordination Note: Flagged potential glideslope RF coupling for joint multi-agent arbitration review.

airspace_safety.observation: Aircraft SYN123 is in final_approach on ILS CAT II at 450 ft AGL. 5G Cell CELL-17 is 900 m from runway threshold (300 m lateral offset). 3D slant separation distance is 954.7 m.
airspace_safety.assessment: Simulated baseline altimeter margin is +42.1 dB (minimum 6.0 dB required under CLM-106). A dynamic power boost (+3 dB) reduces margin to +39.1 dB, which violates glide path safety. Antenna downtilt (3°) safely restores margin to +46.6 dB (SIMULATION) while preserving cell coverage.

2. PFD Simulation (CLM-109): Baseline margin = +42.1 dB; +3 dB boost drops margin to +39.1 dB.
3. Glideslope Safety Standard (CLM-106): Enforcing strict 6.0 dB margin floor. Power increases rejected; downtilt verified safe.
4. Precautionary Guard: Radar altimeter tolerance category is unverified; conservative baseline strictly maintained.

spectrum.observation: 5G Cell CELL-17 operates in band n78 with carriers 3300–3670 MHz. In India, the authorized mid-band 5G spectrum is 3300–3670 MHz under CON-INT-004.
spectrum.assessment: Active band n78 (3300–3670 MHz) complies with national licensing. However, candidate retuning to 4100 MHz (n77) is strictly prohibited: it violates national frequency license CON-INT-004 and abuts the globally protected 4200–4400 MHz aeronautical radionavigation band governed by ITU RR 5.438 (CLM-140). Mandatory 530 MHz separation to radar altimeter band must be strictly preserved.
chain_of_thought: 1. Spectrum Allocation Check: Verified active carriers 3300–3670 MHz within licensed band in India (3300–3670 MHz).
2. Aeronautical Protection: Checked ITU Radio Regulations RR 5.438 and CLM-140; 4200–4400 MHz band has strict exclusive aeronautical allocation.
3. Out-of-Band Emission Review: Enforced CON-INT-001 and CON-INT-004. Proposed 4100 MHz operation flagged as severe non-compliance.
4. Verdict: Authorized n78 operation permitted; 4100 MHz retuning rejected.
spectrum.uncertainty: Exact manufacturer spurious emission filter rolloff curve for cell site gNodeB is unverified.
warnings: 4100 MHz operation violates both national license and proximity boundary

policy_institutional.observation: Scenario jurisdiction is India evaluated as of 2026-10-07. Regulatory authorities include DGCA, Ministry of Civil Aviation, and DoT/WPC. Key instruments identified: DGCA AIC 19/2025 and 5G band licensing conditions.
policy_institutional.assessment: DGCA AIC 19/2025 (CLM-131) has an effective date of 2027-12-31, which is in the future relative to 2026-10-07; it is classified strictly as NOT_YET_IN_FORCE. Under institutional rule CON-IN-004, automated cell reconfigurations that increase emissions near an aerodrome require human ATC / coordinator authorization. Furthermore, GAP-006 notes the absence of numeric runway buffer coordinates in primary circulars, mandating precautionary defaults.
chain_of_thought: 1. Temporal Status Audit: Compared as-of date 2026-10-07 against DGCA AIC 19/2025 effective date (2027-12-31). Formally marked NOT_YET_IN_FORCE.
2. Institutional Authorization (CON-IN-004): Automated RF power boosts near runway approach corridors require human oversight.
3. Policy Gap Identification (GAP-006): Primary circulars lack published numeric exclusion contours around runway thresholds. Precautionary boundary enforced.
4. Verdict: Dynamic power increases require human authorization gate; off-corridor traffic steering (ACT-2) and downtilt (ACT-3) comply with institutional mandates.
policy_institutional.uncertainty: GAP-006: Lack of published numeric exclusion radius around synthetic airport runways in primary circulars.
warnings: DGCA AIC 19/2025 is NOT_YET_IN_FORCE as of 2026-10-07

optimization.assessment: Multi-objective Pareto evaluation identifies Off-Corridor Traffic Steering (ACT-2) as strictly dominant: it relieves 30% PRB congestion by offloading users to CELL-18 (>1200 m away) with 0.0 dB increase in runway emissions.
chain_of_thought: 1. Multi-Objective Formulation: Mapped candidate actions onto 4 objective dimensions (Airspace Margin, PRB Relief, License Compliance, Latency).
2. Geometry & Flight Phase: Aircraft in final_approach at 450 ft AGL, cell at 900 m.
3. Pareto Dominance Evaluation: ACT-2 achieves 0.92 aggregate score; eliminates glideslope interference while recovering QoS.
4. Selection Recommendation: Forwarded ACT-2 as primary preference to arbitration agent.
